item.title: My Dog In Three Places

turns.text: Can you make three square photos of my dog: on a sandy beach, on a snowy forest trail, and in a cosy living room? It should look like this same dog in every one, not just any golden retriever. Keep him natural, no clothes or text.

item.tests: Maintains the individual identity of a reference dog while changing its surroundings across three photorealistic images.

answer_sheet.Dog reference: The golden retriever in dog.jpg; keep his individual facial features, coat colour and build.
answer_sheet.Locations and output count: Three separate photos: a sandy beach, a snowy forest trail, and a cosy living room.
answer_sheet.Style and size: Photorealistic square images; standard free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: Three separate square, photorealistic images are delivered.
The dog's face, ears, muzzle, coat colour and build remain recognisably consistent with dog.jpg in all three.
The locations are visibly a sandy beach, a snowy forest trail, and a cosy living room, one per image.
The dog is naturally integrated into each setting with plausible scale, lighting and ground contact.
The dog wears no clothes and the images contain no text.

turns.text: can you make pics of my dog in this pic

dialog.agent:
Happy to make some pictures of your golden retriever. One question before I start:

**What should change in the picture?**

For example, you could put them somewhere new (a beach or snow), give them an outfit, or change the style (cartoon or painting). I'll keep your dog looking the same, and the pictures will be square like your photo.
dialog.why: The assistant asks the user what should change in the picture and waits for their answer before generating anything.
dialog.user: put him on a sandy beach, a snowy forest trail, and a cosy living room. like 3 separate pics. no clothes or text tho

turns.agent:
I couldn't make the pictures. Magic Hour turned down all three because your account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was created and no links are ready.

I'd already used the cheapest free-plan setup (5 credits per picture), so the three would need about 15 credits. Using a different image tool on the free plan won't help, because they all cost at least as much.

**To get your pictures, you could:**
1. **Add credits.** Your free credits may top up over time, or you can buy a credit pack from your Magic Hour account page.
2. **Then tell me to go ahead.** I'll make the same three pictures: one on a sandy beach, one on a snowy forest trail and one in a cosy living room. Each will be square, keep his look and pose, and have no clothes or text.

If you only have enough credits for one or two, tell me which settings matter most and I'll start with those.
